Remove islands

Source: R/remove_islands.R
remove_islands.Rd

Keeps only the largest group of neighbouring polygons (queen contiguity), i.e. the one with the most polygons, and drops the polygons outside it. This is useful before calling uci() with dist_type = "spatial_link", which requires the polygons to form one contiguous area.

Usage

remove_islands(sf_object, var_name = NULL, showProgress = TRUE)

Arguments

sf_object

A POLYGON sf data.frame.

var_name

An optional string. The name of a numeric column in sf_object. If given, the message also reports how many activities were dropped (NA values are considered to be equal to 0). Only used for the message. Defaults to NULL.

showProgress

A logical. If TRUE (Default), a message reports how many polygons were removed.

Value

sf_object with only the polygons of the largest contiguous group (same CRS, columns, row order and row names).

Details

If several groups tie for the most polygons, the group with the earliest row is kept. Objects with fewer than 2 rows are returned as they are. Contiguity is computed in the CRS of sf_object, which is not changed. uci(remove_islands = TRUE) applies this function after reprojecting to EPSG:3857, so for exactly the same result on geographic (lon/lat) data, reproject sf_object first.

See also

Other urban centrality index: uci()

Examples

# load data
data_dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "uci")
# sf::st_as_sf() loads {sf}, whose methods subset and bind sf objects
grid <- sf::st_as_sf(readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "grid_bho.rds")))

# add an island: a copy of the first cell, shifted away from the grid
island <- grid[1, ]
sf::st_geometry(island) <- sf::st_geometry(island) + c(0.5, 0)
sf::st_crs(island) <- sf::st_crs(grid)
grid_island <- rbind(grid, island)
nrow(grid_island)
#> [1] 899

# remove the island
grid_main <- remove_islands(grid_island, var_name = 'jobs')
#> Removed 1 polygon (180 jobs) outside the largest contiguous area of
#> `sf_object`.
nrow(grid_main)
#> [1] 898
